qt: to the Commission Céline Imart (PPE), Christophe Gomart (PPE) Subject:

With the revision of the European guidelines on regional State aid for 2028-2034, four French territories could become eligible for classification as ‘A’ areas, thus allowing business development projects to benefit from aid rates of up to 30 %. Regional aid is specifically designed to reduce territorial disparities; this update would risk penalising the territories bordering those departments that are classified as ‘C’ areas and have lower aid rates (capped at 15 %). 1.
Will the Commission carry out an assessment of the impact of classifying new areas as ‘A’ areas on economic attractiveness and local employment in neighbouring areas?

Would this assessment consider in particular the risks of distortion of competition, relocation of investments and relocation of activities to the detriment of neighbouring territories with lower aid rates?

Will it put in place compensatory or mitigating measures for these territories in order to maintain their competitiveness, support job retention and creation, and prevent disparities in public support from exacerbating territorial imbalances?
